# DanceAi (C#)

Real-time musical **bar-phase** estimation from a live audio stream, via ONNX.
C# port of the [`dance-ai`](../dance-ai) TypeScript package — same algorithms,
verified against the same golden vectors generated by the Python training
frontend.

This is one of three mirrored implementations of the same streaming inference
contract; they must stay numerically in sync:

- `dance/streaming.py` — Python reference
- `dance-ai/` — TypeScript (browser / node, `onnxruntime-web`/`-node`)
- `dance-ai-csharp/` — this package (.NET, `Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime`)

## Layout

```
dance-ai-csharp/
  src/DanceAi/            class library (the NuGet package)
    MelFrontend.cs          streaming log-mel frontend (exact-size DFT, no FFT padding)
    RunningPeakNormalizer.cs causal level normalization
    PhaseExtrapolator.cs    constant-tempo phase clock (dependency-free)
    DancePhaseEstimator.cs  ONNX inference + carried GRU/LSTM state
    ModelMeta.cs            meta.json schema + FrameEstimate
  tests/DanceAi.Tests/    xUnit tests against dance-ai/test/vectors/
```

## Build, test, pack

```bash
cd dance-ai-csharp

dotnet build                         # build the library
dotnet test                          # run the golden-vector tests
dotnet pack src/DanceAi -c Release   # produce src/DanceAi/bin/Release/DanceAi.0.1.0.nupkg
```

The tests locate `../dance-ai/test/vectors/` at runtime, so the two ports are
checked against identical reference data. Regenerate vectors with
`dance-ai/scripts/gen_test_vectors.py` after any frontend change.

## Publishing (NuGet — the npm equivalent)

NuGet is .NET's package registry. The `.csproj` doubles as the package manifest
(`<PackageId>`, `<Version>`, etc.), `dotnet pack` produces a `.nupkg`, and:

```bash
dotnet nuget push src/DanceAi/bin/Release/DanceAi.0.1.0.nupkg \
  --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json \
  --api-key $NUGET_API_KEY
```

Get the API key from your account on <https://www.nuget.org>. Bump `<Version>`
in `DanceAi.csproj` for each release (the registry rejects re-pushing a version).

## Usage

```csharp
using DanceAi;

// Load the ONNX model + its meta.json sidecar (both from export_onnx.py).
using var estimator = DancePhaseEstimator.FromFiles("phase_gru_mel.onnx", "phase_gru_mel.meta.json");
var extrapolator = new PhaseExtrapolator();

// Feed mono float samples at meta.samplerate (24 kHz) as they arrive.
// Capture them however you like (NAudio, PortAudio, a file, …) — this package
// has no audio-capture dependency (the TS package's AudioWorklet has no C# analog).
foreach (FrameEstimate e in estimator.Feed(monoSamples))
{
    extrapolator.Update(e.Phase, e.BarDurationS);
}

// In your render/clock loop, read the smoothly extrapolated phase:
double phase = extrapolator.PhaseAt();   // [0, 1), 0 = bar start

// On a hard stream restart / device switch:
estimator.Reset();
extrapolator.Reset();
```

Each `FrameEstimate` carries `Phase` (bar phase in [0,1)), `BarDurationS`
(predicted bar duration — tempo), `LogVar` (raw aleatoric uncertainty), and
`ExpectedPhaseError` (derived |phase error| in bars).
